title: Our Last Crusade or the Rise of a New World
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: The Empire and the Nebulis Sovereignty, a nation founded by persecuted users of astral power, have been at war for about a century. Iska, the Empire's youngest Saint Disciple swordsman, and Alice, the Sovereignty's princess and Ice Calamity Witch, meet on the battlefield and are drawn to each other as both seek an end to the war (Yen Press blurb via AniList/MU; ANN review of the light novel).
life_message: Seeing the enemy as a person can open a way to peace that propaganda hides.

content.note: Battlefield sword, gun and magic combat (AniList Military, Guns, Swordplay); ANN describes flashy action without gore (light novel).
Ongoing war; a final battle with a powerful character running amok (ANN, light novel).
Enemies-to-lovers romance; Ecchi genre, Partial Nudity, Sexual Innuendo (MU), Nudity (AniList); ANN notes a nude bathing illustration (light novel).
MU lists 'Traitor Protagonist'; meeting the enemy in secret.
Manga of a light novel franchise with an anime (MU).

dominant: Star-crossed enemies; prejudice and war propaganda; peace through personal contact

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Duels between champions, but leads seek talks at neutral cities (ANN).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Iska bends his strict Empire's rules to meet Alice (ANN, MU Traitor Protagonist).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Loyalty to squad and nation set against personal bond.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Royal and imperial ranks shown, but the story favours the leads' person-to-person meeting.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Conflict framed partly as technology versus magic (ANN).

Survival vs self-expression.evidence: Personal feelings pursued amid a survival war.

folkways.japan: The pairing of rival nations' champions draws on familiar Japanese light-novel romance patterns rather than any specific Japanese social norm.

delivery.evidence: ANN (light novel): anti-prejudice theme carried by the romance, not stated as lessons.

personified.ideology: the enemy is human; end the war through understanding
the same hope from the Sovereignty side

delivery.note: The Empire is described as strict but not wholly repressive, while its leaders' motives are left unexplored.

winners_losers: The leads who question their nations' hostility get the sympathy; war propaganda and the hidden rulers are cast in doubt.
to_verify: The ANN review covers the light novel (vol. 1), not the manga; manga fan service and violence levels to confirm.
